nodes.action: Read the existing implementation and project documentation to identify input shape, required output shape, validation rules, side-effect boundaries, and existing audit or mock interfaces.
nodes.name: Inspect project contract
preconditions: Target project and task documentation are available
nodes.validator: Required fields, optional fields, normalization rules, error schema, and return schema are identified before editing.

nodes.action: Create or reuse a small projection/normalization layer that preserves the original row while exposing normalized values needed for validation and downstream dispatch.
nodes.name: Define normalized row projection
nodes.validator: Normalization is deterministic, makes default policies explicit, and does not silently discard source values.

nodes.action: Evaluate every applicable rule before any external call, collecting all failures for the row rather than stopping at the first failure.
inputs: Previously accepted state when uniqueness matters
nodes.name: Screen each row locally
outputs: Dispatchable valid candidate or rejected row
nodes.validator: Errors identify the relevant field or parameter, reason, observed value when useful, and expected constraint; invalid rows have no outbound side effect.

nodes.action: Iterate through the complete batch in source order, preserve zero-based indices, continue after rejected rows, and dispatch only candidates with no validation errors.
nodes.name: Process batch in order
nodes.validator: Every input row is represented exactly once as either a success or failure, and valid rows are not blocked by invalid rows.

nodes.action: Construct the project’s required structured result, retaining original rejected payloads, detailed errors, side-effect trace, and aggregate counts without changing the public contract.
nodes.name: Build structured audit result
nodes.validator: Return keys and nested error fields match the documented contract; counts reconcile with total input rows.

nodes.action: Run focused checks that valid rows were dispatched, invalid rows were not dispatched, all row-level failures were accumulated, and normalization/default policies are visible where required.
nodes.name: Verify dispatch boundary
nodes.validator: Outbound-call trace contains no rejected row, accepted/rejected partition is complete, and representative multi-error cases retain every applicable failure.

nodes.action: Extract the input shape, required fields, optional fields, normalization rules, outbound-call contract, and required result schema before editing.
nodes.name: Inspect project contract
preconditions: Target project and input batch are available
nodes.validator: Required fields, optionality, and output keys are explicitly identified.

nodes.action: Centralize deterministic local checks, including type, presence, emptiness, format, range, uniqueness, ordering, and timezone normalization rules as applicable.
nodes.name: Define local validation policy
preconditions: Reusable validation and processing contract exists
nodes.validator: Every rejected condition maps to a structured error containing the relevant field or parameter and observed value or comparison context.

nodes.action: Parse each raw item and derive the comparison or API-ready representation without mutating the original payload.
nodes.name: Normalize and project input
nodes.validator: Naive or encoded values are normalized according to the documented policy, while the original item remains available for reporting.

nodes.action: Run all applicable validations for the item and accumulate every failure before deciding whether to dispatch it.
nodes.name: Collect all item errors
outputs: Complete error list or validated candidate
nodes.validator: An item with multiple independent defects reports multiple errors and does not stop at the first failure.

nodes.action: Dispatch only candidates with no validation errors; otherwise record a failure entry containing the original index, original item, and structured errors.
nodes.name: Gate outbound operation
preconditions: Complete error list or validated candidate exists
nodes.validator: No invalid item reaches the external or mock API, and valid items preserve input order.

nodes.action: Build the required return object with successes, failures, trace or audit information, and total/succeeded/failed summary counts.
nodes.name: Aggregate batch outcome
preconditions: Successful results and failure records exist
nodes.validator: Counts reconcile with input length and every failure retains its zero-based index.

nodes.action: Run focused checks covering valid dispatch, local rejection, multiple simultaneous errors, optional fields, normalization edge cases, duplicate or ordering rules, and summary consistency.
nodes.name: Verify behavior
nodes.validator: Checks confirm invalid inputs are rejected before dispatch and valid inputs continue processing independently.
